findings.issue_text: app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 — has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` lacks `embed_in_root: true`, so the sideloaded `embeddable_hosts` array is never emitted at the JSON root, leaving the Ember store's `_hydrateEmbedded` unable to resolve `embeddable_host_ids` into host objects

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — self.host.sub!` in `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when host is nil/blank instead of letting validates_format_of report a validation error, turning bad input into a 500.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:2 — create_table uses force: true with no down/reversible method, so on an irreversible ActiveRecord::Migration this silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table and cannot be rolled back.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:15 — fetch_embedding builds an OpenStruct as a fake model just to satisfy the serializer, an unclear ad-hoc type that leaks presentation shape into the controller instead of using a small PORO/value object.

app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:1 — EmbeddableHostSerializer duplicates the same id/host/category_id attribute logic that EmbeddingSerializer also relies on via embed: :ids, and both controllers (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, embedding_controller.rb) independently render this serializer, risking divergence if the host shape changes.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:26 — Migration interpolates site_settings `embeddable_hosts` values directly into raw SQL INSERT string without escaping, allowing SQL injection if an admin-controlled setting contains a single quote (low practical risk since it's a one-time migration run by admins, but still unsafe raw SQL construction)

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 — has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` lacks `embed_in_root: true`, so the sideloaded `embeddable_hosts` array is never emitted at the JSON root, leaving the Ember store's `_hydrateEmbedded` unable to resolve `embeddable_host_ids` into host objects

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbeddingSerializer` uses `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids`, but it does not show how `render_serialized(..., rest_serializer: true)` / the app’s serializer adapter is configured (e.g., global `embed_in_root`/include behavior). Without that context, it’s not verifiable from the diff that the sideloaded `embeddable_hosts` collection is “never emitted at the JSON root.” The claim depends on framework configuration not present in the PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — self.host.sub!` in `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when host is nil/blank instead of letting validates_format_of report a validation error, turning bad input into a 500.
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: the before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` to normalize the host, but if `host` is nil (or blank), `sub!` is called on nil and raises a NoMethodError instead of allowing validations to handle it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:2 — create_table uses force: true with no down/reversible method, so on an irreversible ActiveRecord::Migration this silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table and cannot be rolled back.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, risking data loss. The migration is also effectively irreversible as written because it uses raw `execute` statements (including deleting site_settings rows) inside `change` without a `down`/`reversible` block, so it cannot be cleanly rolled back.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:15 — fetch_embedding builds an OpenStruct as a fake model just to satisfy the serializer, an unclear ad-hoc type that leaks presentation shape into the controller instead of using a small PORO/value object.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` constructing an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` solely to be rendered via `EmbeddingSerializer` (`render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)`). This is an ad-hoc “fake model” to match the serializer’s expected shape (attributes `:id` and `has_many :embeddable_hosts`), which is a maintainability/architecture concern rather than a concrete correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:1 — EmbeddableHostSerializer duplicates the same id/host/category_id attribute logic that EmbeddingSerializer also relies on via embed: :ids, and both controllers (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, embedding_controller.rb) independently render this serializer, risking divergence if the host shape changes.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, EmbeddingSerializer does not duplicate `id/host/category_id` logic; it only declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`. There is only one place defining the host shape: `EmbeddableHostSerializer`. While that serializer redundantly defines `id/host/category_id` methods that just return `object` fields, the finding’s claim that both serializers/controllers “independently” implement the same shape and risk divergence isn’t supported by the diff (EmbeddingController renders EmbeddingSerializer, which reuses EmbeddableHostSerializer rather than duplicating it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:26 — Migration interpolates site_settings `embeddable_hosts` values directly into raw SQL INSERT string without escaping, allowing SQL injection if an admin-controlled setting contains a single quote (low practical risk since it's a one-time migration run by admins, but still unsafe raw SQL construction)

adjudication.rationale: The migration builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts`. This is unescaped raw SQL; a host containing a single quote could break the query or be leveraged for SQL injection during migration execution.
